articles.title_orig: The US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown it
articles.title_zh: The US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown it
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia’s chips are powering America’s AI boom. Of course Chinese spies are interested.
Nvidia’s chips are powering America’s AI boom. Of course Chinese spies are interested.
As espionage targets go, Jensen Huang is perhaps one of the least surprising on Earth. The Nvidia CEO runs one of the world’s most valuable companies, controls the in-demand technology fueling the AI boom, and is cozy with presidents, CEOs, and all manner of important people. He also wears a cool leather jacket.
Which makes Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy — reportedly while her spying was known to US intelligence and even President Donald Trump — all the more shocking. The fallout goes well beyond his marriage, his reputation, or Nvidia itself. Experts tell The Verge the incident threatens to disrupt the entire US AI industry, potentially jeopardize national security, and could undermine America’s efforts to maintain its fragile technological lead over China in AI.
“With those chips, the US lead could vanish in a matter of weeks or months.”
Nvidia is the undisputed leader in advanced computer chips, among the AI industry’s scarcest resources. While many ingredients go into building AI models — including talent, energy, capital, and data — top-tier chips are one of the most important, and Nvidia is one of a handful of companies with the expertise to design or manufacture them at the cutting edge. That makes it a gatekeeper to hardware that has become a key bottleneck in global AI development. US companies — including Meta, Anthropic, and OpenAI — are racing to develop chips of their own, in part to reduce their dependence on Nvidia, even as they spend billions securing ever more compute.
For China, the US’s main rival at the frontier of AI, that bottleneck is even tighter. To maintain its technological lead, the US has restricted the sale of the most advanced AI chips to the country in the hopes of slowing its progress in the sector, which has been impressive and is thought to trail the US by a matter of months. In response, China has made developing domestic alternatives a strategic national priority, though its leaders still lag Nvidia at the bleeding edge. At the same time, a thriving black market for restricted Nvidia chips has emerged.
Experts tell The Verge that China could exploit access to Nvidia to accelerate its own development, or to impede the US development of AI.
Getting its hands on more Nvidia chips is the most obvious win for Beijing, says Emily Kilcrease, a senior fellow and director of the energy, economics, and security program at the Center for a New American Security (CNAS) think tank. China has advantages in other parts of the AI race — including abundant energy and a solid ecosystem of open weight models — but without the latest Nvidia chips, it “cannot close the gap with US frontier capabilities,” Kilcrease tells The Verge . “With those chips, the US lead could vanish in a matter of weeks or months.”
It is not clear how successful the alleged spying operation has been on that front. There is no public evidence indicating that Huang himself has helped direct restricted Nvidia chips toward China or that sensitive information about them was obtained from him. But companies linked to the alleged spy, Alice Huang — no relation to Jensen — have reportedly enabled at least $7 billion of Nvidia chip sales to China.
Brookings fellow Kyle Chan tells The Verge that a concern for US industry could be that companies with alleged ties to China may have had priority access to Nvidia’s latest GPUs. “In a time of chip scarcity,” that would make it much harder for American companies to access them, Chan says.
Huang is also a prominent critic of American restrictions on chip sales, and Nvidia spends a formidable amount lobbying in Washington. Last year, he successfully secured White House approval to start exporting Nvidia’s H200 AI GPU chips to “approved customers” in China and other countries. Crucially, Huang also has the ear of President Trump as well as other world leaders, giving him great influence over policy decisions.
Hardware is not the only thing of value China could get from close access to Huang, Sunny Cheung, a fellow for China studies at the Jamestown Foundation think tank, tells The Verge . “I actually think too many people are focused on whether somebody managed to steal Nvidia’s trade secrets,” Cheung says, calling it a “very narrow way” of looking at espionage. “I would hope Jensen Huang isn’t foolish enough to hand over the blueprints for Nvidia’s next-generation chips to a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.”
The Nvidia CEO’s relationships with other tech executives, senior policymakers, and Trump himself give him an unusually intimate view into how some of the most powerful people in the US are thinking and planning. Beijing could use information on how American companies are planning major infrastructure expansions, their compute requirements, or broad industry trends to inform its own investments and industrial strategy, Cheung says.
Huang’s intelligence value could extend well beyond AI, too. “That information alone could be extremely valuable,” says Cheung, pointing to insights Beijing could glean into White House thinking about export controls or the private views of Silicon Valley executives on China and Taiwan.
“When so much of America’s AI infrastructure depends on one company, any significant security or governance problem at Nvidia can create uncertainty across the industry.”
But helping China advance is only one side of this equation. Disrupting Nvidia — as this scandal clearly has — could destabilize America’s entire AI industry. More than most companies, Nvidia is remarkably closely tied to the identity and reputation of its rockstar CEO. Huang cofounded the company more than three decades ago, and ever since then he has served as its president, chief executive, and a member of the board of directors. Despite holding a relatively small stake in the company, in many ways Nvidia is Jensen Huang. Nvidia shares have slumped since news of the affair broke.
“When so much of America’s AI infrastructure depends on one company, any significant security or governance problem at Nvidia can create uncertainty across the industry,” Cheung says.
Kilcrease echoes those concerns, warning that the scandal could “destabilize” the company. At the very least, she says the various investigations already underway “will consume an immense amount of bandwidth within the company,” creating a very real risk of weighing down Nvidia’s day-to-day operations. If those distractions begin to affect Nvidia’s ability to execute — slowing decisions, product rollouts, or the allocation of already scarce chips — the consequences could quickly reach customers. The AI labs and hyperscalers such as OpenAI and Anthropic “could have a real issue accessing the vast amounts of compute they need,” Kilcrease says, adding that switching to other hardware “takes time.”
In a race to build increasingly powerful AI, time is a precious resource. Experts say China trails the US closely, meaning that even modest delays for American companies can help Chinese rivals catch up. Nvidia is almost certain to face further disruption as investigations continue, though the extent to which the turmoil will roil the rest of the industry may be difficult to measure.
For China, however, the scandal could be about to backfire spectacularly now everything is out in the open. “The odds of AI chip control legislation being passed in Congress just went through the roof,” Kilcrease says.
Correction, Tuesday November 10th: A sentence in this article misstated that Anthropic is the leader in advanced computer chips. It is Nvidia.

articles.title_orig: Pixel phones getting new icon styles, Create My Widget, and more in November Pixel Drop
articles.title_zh: Pixel phones getting new icon styles, Create My Widget, and more in November Pixel Drop
articles.content_orig:
Google’s Pixel phones get an update every month, but most are just security patches and bug fixes. The bigger changes are bundled into quarterly Pixel Drops, and one is rolling out today . The update brings a few new things, and many of the Gemini features previously exclusive to the latest Pixel phones will also expand to Google’s Pixel 10 lineup.
The Pixel 11 was Google’s first foray into “Gemini Intelligence” branding, something we’ll see a lot more of going forward. Some of the features under that heading were limited to Google’s newest phones (and in some cases, Samsung’s phones). The November Pixel Drop will expand these AI features to the Pixel 10 lineup, but importantly, that doesn’t include the budget-oriented Pixel 10a .
For starters, the Pixel 10 series will get the improved personalized suggestions (previously known as Magic Cue) that debuted on the Pixel 11 . This enables things like sending grocery lists to Google Keep from other apps and generating summaries from the context menu. Rambler, Google’s AI-assisted voice input system, is also coming to the 2025 phones. Likewise, Gemini app automation will roll out on Pixel 10 with this update. This feature is still limited to select apps in rideshare, food delivery, travel, and a few other categories.
The AI-powered icon theming that Google added to Pixels back in March is also getting an update. Initially, this feature just matched icon colors to the system theme when developers didn’t include the necessary theming assets. With this update, Google says it has moved the feature to a more powerful Nano Banana model, unlocking 10 new icon styles for your home screen.
The update also brings Create My Widget to Pixel phones. Google announced this earlier in 2026 , and it shipped on Googlebooks a few weeks ago. The idea is that you describe a home screen widget you want, and Android builds it for you on the spot. However, the use cases are pretty narrow. You’re limited to data accessible in search (e.g., stock prices, sports scores, and weather) and select Google account data points like Gmail or your calendar.
So that’s a lot of AI. Google does have some non-AI additions with this update, but don’t get your hopes up. One of the headlining additions is (drumroll) HiLight support for Google Messages. Yes, Pixel 11 phones will be able to illuminate HiLight when you get a message from important contacts. Ignoring that we had more functional notification LEDs 20 years ago, this is a good and necessary improvement for Google’s least useful hardware feature.
If you have a Pixel Watch, Google says this update will also improve your workout routine. The Pixel Watch 3 and newer will be able to display step-by-step guidance for your workouts. The wearable can also log reps and weights as you go without interrupting live metrics. While Create My Widget is not yet available on the watch, Google promises it’s also coming soon.
The update is beginning its rollout today and should be available widely in the coming days.

Long-pressing on your homescreen reveals a tweaked design for the menu pop-up where the carousel appears first. Going to Wallpaper & style > Color reveals a new paint palette icon that gives you the “Select a color” slider to choose the main accent after previously being limited to presets. On the Pixel 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold, HiLight now supports message notifications — blinking twice — after launching with just calls and Gemini status. Go to Settings > System > HiLight for the new “Messages from favorites: Glows when your favorite contacts send you messages.” When you go to Google Contacts, the HiLight sheet shows individual options for Phone calls and Messages.
When you’re charging or Battery Saver is enabled, there’s now an outline around the battery icon in Quick Settings. Additionally, it’s now Settings > Battery & charging for a more unified menu as introduced on the Pixel 11 series.
In Quick Settings, there are new Tiles for Audio streams and Voice broadcast. A bigger update that lets you customize the arrangement of the brightness slider and media player is not launching with this release.
The new Status bar customization in Settings > System lets you control which Notification icons appear (All, Priority, or None), as well as System icons:

Android 17 QPR2 is rolling out starting today for the Pixel 6a, Pixel 7, Pixel 7 Pro, Pixel 7a, Pixel Tablet, Pixel Fold, Pixel 8, Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 8a, Pixel 9, Pixel 9 Pro, Pixel 9 Pro XL, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel 9a, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, Pixel 10a, Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

The Android Beta Program will remain open and continue testing QPRs and feature drops.
To get the stable version, those running the Android 17 QPR2 Beta have to opt out first . Devices will not be wiped by the stable OTA once that becomes widely available.

articles.title_zh: Greta Thunberg warns ‘everything we love is at stake’ as she arrives at UN climate talks
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in

Prominent climate change activist Greta Thunberg arrived Tuesday at the U.N. climate meeting, where she emphasized the need to protect people and the planet over profits and power.
This year's meeting — called the Conference of the Parties, or COP31 — comes after a year of climate-induced heat waves and other disasters.
As she arrived at the meeting venue in Antalya , Turkey, Thunberg said climate change is “threatening everything" and that “everything and everyone we love is at stake.”
“We should act to protect and benefit people rather than constantly sacrificing the global majority and the very planet we are all living on, for a fortunate few to keep making unimaginable profits and maintaining geopolitical power,” she told reporters.
Thunberg is attending her first U.N. climate summit since she participated in the 2021 COP in Glasgow , Scotland , where she dismissed promises made by global leaders as “blah, blah, blah."
In 2024, Thunberg participated in a protest rally in Georgia against Azerbaijan hosting that year's climate talks. Thunberg accused Azerbaijan of using that summit to "greenwash their crimes and human rights abuses.”
Thunberg is expected to join this year's talks for a few days. She said structural changes are needed across the world to deal with the climate crisis because current political and economic systems “have become incompatible with human nature.”
Arasu reported from Bengaluru, India.

articles.title_orig: Queen's Son, on House Arrest, Alleges an Attack
articles.title_zh: Queen's Son, on House Arrest, Alleges an Attack
articles.content_orig:
When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.
Queen Mette-Marit's 29-year-old son, Marius Borg Høiby , has been on house arrest at Skaugum Palace since he was convicted for rape in June, and on Friday, November 6, an intruder broke into the royal residence and attacked him.
Per Norwegian media outlet Se og Hor , King Haakon's stepson—who lives in a separate house on the royal estate—was painting and listening to music when an unknown man "tried to enter the home by kicking in the door." Høiby, who reportedly "didn't understand what was happening," opened the door and was pushed by the intruder.
Høiby was able to force the man outside and police arrived in less than two minutes, per Se og Hor . According to Norwegian media outlet NRK , Høiby's house is located outside the zone covered by the royal security team.
Marius Borg Høiby left house arrest on September 9 for King Harald's funeral. | Credit: Getty Images
Høiby arrived at the funeral with Princess Martha Louise's three daughters. | Credit: Getty Images
Høiby, who is Queen Mette-Marit's son from a prior relationship and does not hold a royal title, has been on house arrest at Skaugum Palace for the past 16 weeks. He was found found guilty of 34 offenses ranging from rape to domestic abuse and drug-related offenses, among others.
"We can confirm that we arrested a person near Høiby's home on Friday night," Eirik Veum of the Norwegian Police Security Service told NRK. "Beyond that, we have no comment."
Høiby's defense attorney, Alexander Greaker, told Se og Hor that his client had experienced a "very serious and very unpleasant" situation in his home.
"It is a place where you should feel safe, and in the situation Marius is in right now, it is easy to understand that he has experienced this as very unpleasant and unsafe," Greaker added.

articles.title_orig: Dublin: Arrests made after visit from former US President Biden
articles.title_zh: Dublin: Arrests made after visit from former US President Biden
articles.content_orig:
Hundreds of women have come forward with abuse allegations against the former Harrods and Ritz Paris owner
French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse.
The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released.
In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities.
It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner.
Mohamed Al Fayed accused of multiple rapes by staff
Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor's office said.
It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into "allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape".
The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed.
The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family.
The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson.
The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims:
"At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities.
"In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-ThÃ©rÃ¨se in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators.
"Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations.
"The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office."
A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation.
The Ritz hotel in Paris is still owned by the Al Fayed family
Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024.
One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence.
Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.
A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother , Salah Fayed, who died in 2010.
Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations.
Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate.
In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims.
"Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further."
The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities.
"We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said.
"We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated."
The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like.
"Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over."
The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it "does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour" and that it was ready "to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities".
If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line .

articles.title_orig: Anti-gay laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
articles.title_zh: Anti-gay laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
articles.content_orig:
A UK court has overturned laws criminalising same-sex intimacy in Trinidad and Tobago.
London's Judicial Committee of the Privy Council (JCPC), the Caribbean island's final court of appeal, ruled the laws were not in keeping with the "fundamental individual right to respect for private and family life."
The judgement is the result of an 11-year legal battle brought by dual-citizen Jason Jones, 62, who said he hoped it would "accelerate the fight for full equality."
Jones had successfully challenged the laws in 2018 in Trinidad's High Court, however the ruling was overturned on appeal by the Trinidadian government.
It is the first time the JCPC has ever decided on a case to decriminalise same-sex intimacy, and campaigners hope it will spark similar successful legal challenges elsewhere in the Commonwealth.
Prior to this historic decision, Trinidad and Tobago was one of some 34 Commonwealth countries continuing to criminalise homosexuality based on colonial-era British laws.
Under these laws, consensual same-sex intimacy is punishable by imprisonment, and in some cases carries the death penalty.
The Attorney General of Trinidad and Tobago had argued that the law was protected from legal challenges by the "savings law clauses" - which carried over existing British laws into newly independent states.
Representatives for Jones argued that the laws violated an individual's right to privacy and argued the government's changes to the laws in 1986 - which saw stricter punishments introduced - meant the savings clause protections no longer applied.
The judicial committee unanimously found in favour of Jones.
Handing down the judgement, Lord Sales told the court the laws "cannot be regarded as reasonably justifiable in a society that has a proper respect for the rights and freedoms of an individual".
Jones, human rights campaigner and appellant in the appeal, said: "These laws never reflected who we are as a people and a nation - diverse, multiracial, and secular.
"They told LGBTQ+ people that we were criminals in our own country. That message ends today."
Lawyer Anand Ramlogan SC, representing Jones, said the judgement was a "landmark victory for gay rights, equal dignity and respect for private and family life in Trinidad and Tobago."

articles.title_orig: Side Effects Guaranteed in the First DLC For The Outer Worlds 2, Coming December 2
articles.title_zh: Side Effects Guaranteed in the First DLC For The Outer Worlds 2, Coming December 2
articles.content_orig:
A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the ship’s crew in suspended animation. All signs point to foul play, especially the puddle of what was most likely a person. You recover a video message left by the captain of the vessel, who explains that the crew has been contaminated with something while on a heist that will cause explosive cell death unless they find a cure. And by explosive cell death, she means more like a… “liquefaction”.
By the looks of the puddle on the floor: liquefaction indeed.
The stakes are set for the release of the first of a two-part narrative DLC expansion of The Outer Worlds 2 on December 2. In Side Effects Guaranteed , the video message you found leads you to Gordon Hazen, one of the leading agents in Sub Rosa, a criminal organization made up of like-minded individuals who have chosen to live their lives stealing from the various factions instead of working for them. Gordon in turn sends you to Elysium Valley, a new region on Eden that is home to a settlement of former Protectorate subjects that have been forgotten by their Protectorate leaders. He believes they may have the answers to saving his crew. He personally favors diplomacy over violence but needs you to do whatever you need to in order to get the information he needs.
But Gordon isn’t the only one with interest in Elysium Valley. Another Sub Rosa agent, Algernon Lankester, wants to recruit you to help him exploit the subjects for his own personal gain. The fate of the subjects, the frozen Sub Rosa agents, and the future of Sub Rosa itself is up for you, our intrepid Commander, to decide.
A new narrative story is not all that will be coming when Side Effects Guaranteed launches in a few weeks, however.
Along with the new region of Elysium Valley to explore, players will encounter new threats like vicious canids and primal sprats. What’s a primal sprat? Just a normal sprat, but about 100 times the size. Surely, they’re just as friendly and forgiving of all the time you “accidentally” shot their much smaller cousins while exploring Arcadia.
With these new threats comes the ability to make your Commander even stronger and, of course, more flawed (but in a good way). The level cap will increase from 30 to 36, bringing more skill points to broaden your build. Being able to go to level 36 also means there are three more perks you can acquire, with 15 brand new perks being added into the mix.
Four new flaws will also be introduced that can change how your Commander plays, like “Lethally Tolerant,” a flaw that recognizes your built-up resistance to chemicals so your max toxicity will increase. This is great in the moment, but if you ever experience a Toxicity Crash, you will die instantly. Another example is “Must Have Been the Wind,” which will mark an “assassination target” for a combat group. Killing the target will grant a 20% damage and speed buff until the combat ends, but failing to do so or attacking someone who isn’t the target applies a 10% damage and speed debuff to the player for 30 seconds. Truly rewards that come with great risks.
Side Effects Guaranteed will also see new weapons, new armors, and new outfits for each of the companions, as well as a brand-new Sub Rosa-run radio station featuring 20 new songs for the game. For those who want to jump straight to the action in the DLC, a new alternate starting point is being added to the main menu when you choose a new game that will allow you to start with a custom save that lands you at the start of the DLC. Start the game, allot your skill and perk points, and enjoy Side Effects Guaranteed right away!
This jam-packed adventure with a deep story and systems to build your ideal commander will set up the next DLC for The Outer Worlds 2 that will be coming in Spring of 2027, and choices made will directly impact the next DLC. Part one of this overarching expansion story, Side Effects Guaranteed , will release on December 2 for $14.99, or is available in the Premium Edition or Premium Edition Upgrade for The Outer Worlds 2 .

articles.title_orig: Nvidia Is Down 30% From Its High. History Says This Is What Happens Next.
articles.title_zh: Nvidia Is Down 30% From Its High. History Says This Is What Happens Next.
articles.content_orig:
From the all-time high it hit about a month ago, Nvidia ( NVDA -6.57% ) has lost 30% of its value, and has lost its status as the most valuable company in the world.
This isn't the first time Nvidia stock has plummeted. Based on how it has performed historically, here's what is likely to happen next.
It's hard to believe that just four years ago, Nvidia was a relatively obscure tech company making graphics processing units (GPUs) primarily for the video game and crypto-mining markets. But when the generative artificial intelligence (AI) revolution arrived, it had the proprietary technology to power that software ready and waiting, and it has provided the foundation beneath nearly all successful AI development.
Amid the rapid build-out of data centers capable of supporting powerful AI, Nvidia has exploded. Companies like Alphabet and Space Exploration Technologies are pouring billions into AI and data center development, and a big chunk of that spending goes to Nvidia. In fact, on SpaceX's most recent earnings call, CEO Elon Musk said his company would be "exclusive" to Nvidia, because "the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture."
SpaceX also just announced that it has committed funding for the biggest GPU financing deal ever , and since SpaceX is exclusively using Nvidia GPUs, that's where the money is going.
There's been a general tech sell-off over the past week as the market has digested the midterm election results. The S&P 500 , which has become increasingly tech-weighted as its largest components are all tech companies, is down 2.6% since Wednesday, while the even more tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite is down 3.1%. The market anticipates that the incoming Congress could be more hostile to unfettered AI development than the current one, and several incoming governors, among them Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, have already announced that they plan to place moratoriums on data center build-outs in their states until their legislatures act to put more robust protections and regulations in place.
Nvidia, though, has been getting hammered for a completely different reason: CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman who is now being investigated as an alleged Chinese asset. The company and the FBI are investigating, and it's likely that the stock has not seen its bottom from this development as of this writing.
There are no guarantees about what will happen next, especially because the spy-affair story is both unprecedented for the company and still developing. Meanwhile, Nvidia stock has been dropping like a brick. This isn't simply a case of a tech sell-off that we can expect to be followed by reviving investor confidence as external headwinds ease. But investors can look to history to get a sense of what's likely to come.
Let's look back at Nvidia's history over the past five years -- the period when it became more significant as part of the tech economy. Nvidia fell by at least 20% on five separate occasions over that span, including the current slump. Here's how much it fell each time, and where the stock was 12 months later, or for this year, through today:
In each case, it didn't take too long for the stock to rebound fully and then rise much, much higher. Over the past five years, including all the dips, Nvidia stock has gained more than 500%.
NASDAQ · As of 2:58 PM ET 11/10/26
Is the current slump any different? It's not likely. Nvidia is still at the center of AI development, and even if there are ramifications for Nvidia due to shifts in the political landscape or issues for Huang himself due to his affair, the company he co-founded still has loads of growth potential.
Right now, Wall Street is expecting that Nvidia will deliver 90% sales growth overall this year and 68% growth next year. It is possible that its revenue growth rate will underperform next year if government impediments to the data center build-out lead hyperscalers, neoclouds, and other tech players to trim back their orders, but Nvidia still makes the AI chips of choice for the biggest data center operators. History is on Nvidia's side, and even if it takes the company more than 12 months to bounce back from this correction, it's likely to happen eventually.

articles.title_orig: Smart ring maker Oura to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million
articles.title_zh: Smart ring maker Oura to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million
articles.content_orig:
Oura announced on Tuesday that it’s acquiring AI-native primary care company Counsel Health for $625 million. The deal comes a few weeks after Oura postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.”
Counsel Health is an AI-powered healthcare platform that combines a chat-based medical experience with access to licensed physicians. Its service was integrated into the Oura app in June.
Users can connect with Counsel’s medical AI to get personalized medical advice, and chat with a physician when needed, all within the Oura app. Now, the companies plan to expand on their existing partnership to build across preventative care, acute care, and specialty and chronic care.
While Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, rivals like RingConn and Ultrahuman are emerging to dethrone it, putting pressure on the company to keep innovating. By acquiring Counsel Health, Oura is looking to expand its business and help users access medical care.
“Oura helps members understand their physiology and, with Counsel, they can take action on their health across a range of needs, from quick questions and prescriptions to lab results, chronic care, and referrals,” said Oura CEO Tom Hale in a press release .
Counsel Health raised a $25 million Series A a year ago, led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and GV. PitchBook estimates it had raised a total of $36 million.
Following the acquisition, Oura says Counsel will continue serving existing and new enterprise partners, with the goal of expanding its AI-native care model to more people beyond Oura’s membership.
Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer, alongside the company’s 70 employees, Bloomberg reports.
“At Counsel, we’ve built medical AI around trust, safety and responsibility, keeping physicians in the loop for clinical decisions,” Alagappan said in the press release. “Oura’s data gives clinicians objective context, trended biometrics, and member engagement to deliver more informed care. From the start, our teams bonded over a joint vision, shared culture, and mission, further solidifying as we negotiated our deal over the past few months.”
The deal is expected to close before the end of 2027.
Oura also announced that its revenue grew 153% year-over-year to $533 million for the quarter ended on September 30. For its fiscal year 2026, Oura generated revenue of approximately $1.75 billion, marking 92% year-over-year growth.
The company reached an $11 billion valuation following a $900 million late-stage funding round in October 2025.

articles.title_orig: Three China-Nexus Espionage Campaigns Linked Through Sparrow Malware Ecosystem
articles.title_zh: Three China-Nexus Espionage Campaigns Linked Through Sparrow Malware Ecosystem
articles.content_orig:
Three distinct threat activity clusters with shared infrastructure and malware code similarities have been observed targeting telecommunications providers, government organizations, military entities, research institutions, and critical infrastructure across Latin America, Asia, and Europe over the past year.
Check Point Research is tracking the clusters under the names SilentDelivery , OceanGate , and DarkWire . Although initially assumed to be independent sets of attacks, each with its own backdoors and post-exploitation tooling, they have all been linked through a malware ecosystem called Sparrow.
The entity behind the Sparrow framework has been codenamed CopperDragon , and is assessed to be a digital quartermaster developing tools for China-nexus threat actors, including FamousSparrow , Earth Estries , Tropic Trooper , UAT-9244 , and UAT-8302 .
"Each cluster employed a different toolset and different initial access techniques, including compromising internet-facing infrastructure and highly selective watering hole attacks," Check Point said in a technical report published today. "The compromised websites that were used for watering hole attacks were of government, shipping, and IT and research sectors."
Attacks mounted by FamousSparrow are known for deploying backdoors like SparrowDoor (and its variants Crowdoor and TernDoor ), SparroWocky , and HemiGate . It's also assessed to share some degree of overlap with Salt Typhoon. However, the precise nature of the relationship remains unclear.
The cyber espionage ecosystem linked to CopperDragon is driven by three prominent clusters -
The SilentDelivery chain begins with the attacker injecting heavily obfuscated JavaScript into legitimate websites frequented by their intended targets. Visitors to the sites are greeted by a Google Chrome SSL certificate warning that instructs users to install a "Certificate Fix" utility to restore access.
The so-called utility, once deployed, delivers either SquadC or a SparrowDoor variant. All the compromised websites have been found to be related to government, shipping, IT, and research sectors in the Czech Republic, Germany, France, Taiwan, Nepal, Hong Kong, and Indonesia.
According to a report published by Positive Technologies in August 2026, there are indications that the campaign has also targeted entities in Egypt and the Philippines using this method.
"The JavaScript injected into the compromised websites is heavily obfuscated using jsjiami, a publicly available JavaScript obfuscation service," Check Point said. "It first checks whether the user is running Windows and, in some cases, verifies that the website’s domain matches the intended compromised domain."
The script then repeatedly sends status-check requests to a command-and-control (C2) server to fingerprint the user based on IP and geolocation, and ultimately decide whether to continue the attack and serve the fake warning.
Written in C/C++, SquadC is a Windows backdoor that enables initial foothold over the infected host. It establishes persistence by means of a Windows Registry Run key that masquerades as a Windows update assistant. Further analysis has uncovered that the malware is also distributed via phishing emails targeting Indonesian organizations.
The phishing email comes with a Windows Shortcut (LNK) disguised as a PDF document, which, when opened, abuses the legitimate "ftp.exe" binary to run a batch script that's responsible for displaying an empty file as a decoy, while launching SquadC via DLL sideloading.
The OceanGate operation, on the other hand, has been observed targeting both Windows and Linux environments, deploying previously undocumented tooling to maintain access, move laterally across the network, and exfiltrate sensitive data.
The Linux phase of the attack involves two new backdoors -
"After harvesting credentials from multiple users and establishing a strong foothold in the Linux environment, the actor moved into the Windows environment," Check Point explained. "The actor attempted to log in to several Windows machines over RDP, trying different passwords until it successfully authenticated with an administrator account."
This step is followed by the deployment of bespoke post-exploitation tools and a variant of SparrowDoor -
What's more, the threat actor has been found incorporating kernel rootkits and kernel-level access capabilities into SparrowDoor and SparrowShell to evade defenses through process hiding and to capture and manipulate network packet capture using WinDivert drivers.
"The actor abused the driver to convert SparrowDoor into a passive backdoor that intercepts and manipulates packets at the kernel level, making its traffic less visible," Check Point said. "This allows the backdoor to listen internally on one port while receiving connections through an externally accessible port, such as 443, that is already used by a legitimate service."
"The backdoor applies a strict filter to intercept connections from a specific source IP address to the legitimate service's port. It manipulates the packet and rewrites the destination port to the backdoor’s internal listening port, typically a high port such as 49628. For response traffic, it rewrites the source port back to the external service port, making the responses appear to originate from the legitimate service."
Interestingly, SparrowShell shares code- and infrastructure-level similarities with a malware called Mélofée that was first described by ExaTrack in March 2023 as based on the open-source Reptile rootkit. This has raised the possibility that CopperDragon is also behind the development and supply of Mélofée.
The third and last cluster of activity centers around Latin America, with a particular focus on telecommunications operators and government entities. These attacks led to the deployment of two newly identified backdoors called CopperDoor and CopperDNS as a possible replacement for SparrowDoor.
Also supporting these operations is a set of custom tools -
"The operation heavily relies on DLL sideloading as a primary execution technique, often abusing executables that are not widely observed among other threat actors in the wild," Check Point said. "To minimize their footprint, the operators deliberately avoided creating new directories on disk, instead placing their tools within existing system paths."
"CopperDoor infrastructure demonstrated a higher level of operational security. Most IP addresses were located in Latin America, often within the same country as the victim organization. This proximity likely helps the malicious traffic blend in with legitimate network activity and reduces the chances of detection."

articles.title_orig: Stocks, Bonds Fall as CPI Data Fuel Fed-Hike Bets: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Stocks, Bonds Fall as CPI Data Fuel Fed-Hike Bets: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
Stocks fell on Tuesday after October inflation data came in hotter than expected and a key Federal Reserve official hinted at the possibility of a half-point rise in rates next month.
The S&P 500 traded down 0.6%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 181 points, or 0.3%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.1%.
Nvidia dragged down the three major averages, falling 6%. The stock sat out Monday's tech-fueled rally following CEO Jensen Huang's admission over the weekend to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy .
The consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, above the gain of 0.3% that economists polled by Dow Jones expected. Core CPI — which excludes volatile food and energy costs — increased 0.3% in October, whereas economists had called for a 0.2% advance. Annual figures were not be provided for Tuesday's report because of the 2025 government shutdown.
Treasury yields jumped as traders reacted to the report, fearing that interest rate increases could now be more likely in 2027. The 10-year Treasury note yield in particular advanced back above 5% .
Earlier Tuesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech in London that he thinks a December rate hike is likely and opened the door for a possible half-point increase amid persistent  inflationary pressures.
"While the precise timing of the hikes doesn't matter, ensuring that the promised hikes are implemented in a reasonable period of time does," he said.
Traders now see a December rate hike as a near certainty and a small chance of a supersized increase. They also expect at least a quarter-point hike at some point next year.
"There's an extrapolation that maybe the Fed's going to have to hike rates more aggressively next year," said Tom Hainlin, national investment strategist at U.S. Bank Asset Management. He later added, "The CPI print said perhaps inflation is going to be a little stickier for a little longer."
Tuesday's retreat came one day after the S&P 500 posted its best day since April. The push and pull come after a rocky week for markets, in which traders grew concerned about the potential for a slowdown in data center buildouts after Democrats posted big victories in the midterm elections.
Citi upgraded the tokenization stock Securitize while maintaining its $14 price target on the shares, following the company's third quarter earnings Monday evening and announced expansion into asset-backed finance.
Shares were up nearly 20% in afternoon trading.
"Management 3Q commentary provided greater visibility into SECZ's monetization opportunity across token issuance, servicing, trading, stablecoin infrastructure, and credit origination through the pending River One acquisition," Citi analyst Peter Christiansen said in a note Tuesday. "Although we lower near-term profitability expectations following higher-than-expected nonrecurring operating expenses, we come away from the quarter with greater conviction that SECZ is expanding its role across multiple layers of the tokenization value chain … The valuation has become more attractive, supporting our upgrade to Buy/HR."
For more on Securitize's earnings, read our story and watch our exclusive interview with CEO Carlos Domingo here .
The national average price of regular gasoline fell below $4 a gallon for the first time since July , reaching $3.978 a gallon on Tuesday.
Prices are down about 17 cents from a week ago and 39 cents from a month ago, according to AAA . Lower crude prices and normal autumn seasonality have contributed to the decline.
Brent briefly fell below $90 a barrel in hopes of easing U.S.-Iran tensions and recovering oil flows around the Strait of Hormuz.
The Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, however, warned Tuesday that earlier energy shocks may continue affecting prices into 2027.
"While I am pleased to see energy prices down from their high rates over the past week or so, they are still quite elevated relative to the start of the year, and the ultimate effect on inflation will depend on what levels are sustained," he said.
Although further interest-rate increases could pressure bond prices in the near term, Wells Fargo strategists believe today's higher yields offer more income and a stronger starting point for long-term returns.
The firm examined five-, seven- and 10-year periods and found that the relationship between starting yields and subsequent annualized returns was strongest over approximately seven years. Higher income may also help cushion bond-price declines when market rates rise.
"Investors do not need to wait for the peak in interest rates to find opportunities in fixed income," wrote Luis Alvarado, co-head of global fixed-income strategy at Wells Fargo Investment Institute.
Wells Fargo favors short- and intermediate-term bonds, which offer attractive income without the greater interest-rate sensitivity of longer maturities. High-quality bonds may also provide diversification, reduce portfolio volatility and support cash-flow planning.
Separately, the firm remains neutral on information technology following the October sell-off while favoring communication services, industrials and materials as broader beneficiaries of AI investment.
Check out CNBC's live blog to read more about the stocks making midday moves here .
— John Melloy, Deena Zaidi and Darla Mercado
Nike is hosting its first Investor Day since 2017 next week under a new management team led by CEO Elliott Hill.
The event could serve as a crucial moment for the company that has been struggling to turn its business around.
"Next week will be an opportunity for management to signal the pathway ahead for Nike's medium-term growth story," Bernstein analyst Aneesha Sherman wrote in a Tuesday research note.
Investors are weighing up when the sportswear's business will stabilize from stagnating sales and lack of product innovation.
In the foreseeable future, analysts estimate Nike's five-year sales growth "will likely be flattish."
Bernstein sees Fiscal year 2027 as a "reset" in the Lifestyle category modeling a mid-teens decline, while Nike's other core segment, Performance grows 10%.
While the event itself may not be a catalyst for the stock which has gained 12% over the last month, Bernstein said it could "drive incremental investor confidence of a multi-year recovery."
The yield on the 10-year Treasury note jumped on Tuesday, moving back above the key 5% level, after hotter-than-expected inflation data .
The yield climbed more than 14 basis points to 5.004%. It last traded above the 5% level earlier this month. Read more .
Dallas Federal Reserve President Lorie Logan said Tuesday that she expects two more interest rate hikes will be needed as the central bank struggles to bring inflation lower.
"Tighter policy will be necessary to appropriately balance the outlook and risks for inflation and employment. And it is important to achieve that balance promptly," the policymaker said during an energy conference in Houston. "The longer above-target inflation persists, the greater the risk that it becomes baked into behavior."
Earlier in the day, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he expects a quarter percentage point hike would be appropriate at the next policy meeting in December. He even raised the notion that the Fed may have to raise by half a point should inflation numbers come in higher than expected, as they did in Tuesday's consumer price index report.
However, Logan said she thinks two more quarter-point moves would be appropriate before the Fed could take a break.
"The exact pace of increases could depend on the near-term economic and financial environment," she said. "After two more increases are in place, it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate. The goal should be to make policy modestly restrictive so we can sustainably deliver both maximum employment and stable prices."
Logan is a voter this year on the rate-setting Federal Open Market

articles.title_orig: China calls for stronger dialogue, cooperation with France
articles.title_zh: China calls for stronger dialogue, cooperation with France
articles.content_orig:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Tuesday called for stronger dialogue and cooperation with France to deepen political mutual trust and jointly address global risks and challenges, state media reported.
During a telephone conversation with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, Wang said Beijing was ready to work with Paris to fulfill their responsibilities as permanent members of the UN Security Council.
The two countries should also work together to safeguard the common interests of the international community, Wang said, according to state-run Xinhua News Agency.
He expressed hope that France would "honor its commitment to the 'one-China principle' through concrete actions and safeguard the political foundation of China-France relations."
Wang also urged the EU to work with China to establish "stable and balanced" trade relations, emphasizing their importance as major trading partners.
The two sides "stand to gain from cooperation and lose from confrontation," he said.
Barrot, for his part, said France attached great importance to China's status as a major country and remained committed to the one-China policy, according to Xinhua.
He added that Paris was ready to play an active role in promoting dialogue and cooperation between the EU and China.
The two ministers also exchanged views on issues of mutual concern, including the election of the UN secretary-general.
Separately, Wang held talks with Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar in Beijing on Tuesday.
Wang said China was ready to work with Slovakia to advance a vision of global governance based on extensive consultation, joint contributions and shared benefits.
He also called for jointly building a community with a shared future for humanity, according to Xinhua.
Blanar reaffirmed Slovakia's commitment to the one-China policy and described Beijing as an important partner.
He said Slovakia would continue working to provide a stable and favorable environment for Chinese companies to invest and cooperate in the country.

articles.content_orig:
By SHAUN WOOLLER, EXECUTIVE HEALTH EDITOR
Published: 17:00 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 03:22 EST, 9 November 2026
The Daily Mail today launches a major appeal to fund a pioneering support network for unpaid dementia carers as a damning poll reveals two-thirds feel abandoned.
Dementia Carers Together aims to raise millions of pounds for new nationwide six-week courses for friends and relatives of people living with the disease.
Delivered in partnership with Alzheimer's Society, the sessions will give carers vital support and information about their rights and the services available to them.
They will allow attendees to meet others in a similar situation and help to address the loneliness, exhaustion and overwhelming responsibilities many face following a loved one's diagnosis.
There are currently 2.5 million people in the UK who provide some form of care for people with dementia, and four out of five of them have reached crisis point at least once.
Exclusive new polling for the Daily Mail reveals 66 per cent of people who provide or have provided unpaid care to someone with dementia do not feel well supported in their caring role.
The YouGov survey found most people (72 per cent) would not feel confident knowing where to turn for advice if a friend or relative was diagnosed with dementia, and three-quarters (76 per cent) would not feel prepared to cope with behaviour changes such as anger, distress or confusion.
There is also a worrying lack of understanding about what dementia care the NHS and councils will pay for and what support the carers themselves may be entitled to receive.
Michelle Dyson, chief executive of Alzheimer's Society, said it is 'deeply concerning' that seven in ten people are not confident they would know where to turn for advice if a loved one was diagnosed with dementia
The appeal is being co-ordinated by Mail Force, a registered charity set up by the Daily Mail's parent company, DMGT.
Mail Force raised over £35million in its previous campaigns to provide laptops for schoolchildren and PPE during the Covid-19 pandemic, and to help Ukrainian refugees.
The new Dementia Carers Together courses will be held across the UK and consist of six weekly sessions lasting two hours each.
They will offer practical help in dealing with loved ones as they deteriorate, ranging from managing danger at home to navigating changes in hygiene and dealing with confusion.
Other sessions will cover unlocking support, including what you are entitled to medically and financially, such as the right to a timely diagnosis, benefits allowances and council tax reductions.
The courses will also focus on emotional resilience. Carers will be taught ways to cope with the toll on their mental health, how to recognise burnout and stress, and when and how to ask for help.
People can attend all six sessions or only those on the topics of most interest to them. Some will be in-person and some held online, to maximise the opportunity for carers to attend.
Ted Verity, Editor-in-Chief of the Daily Mail, said: 'It is a privilege to work with Alzheimer's Society on tackling an issue that impacts the day-to-day lives of so many people across the UK.
'Every day, millions of dementia carers put somebody else's needs before their own. They do so with extraordinary love, patience and dedication, often while receiving little support themselves.
'Through Dementia Carers Together, Daily Mail readers have an opportunity to make a real difference to the lives of those carers.
'Together, we can create a nationwide support network that offers practical help, trusted advice and the reassurance that nobody has to face dementia alone.'
Michelle Dyson, chief executive of Alzheimer's Society, added: 'It is deeply concerning that seven in ten people are not confident they would know where to turn for advice if a loved one was diagnosed with dementia.
'Families can face difficult and unfamiliar challenges following a diagnosis, and we must make sure they have the support they need to face them.
'That is why the Dementia Carers Together Appeal is so important.
'Our ambition is to create a national network where carers can get practical advice, understand their rights and connect with people who truly understand what they are going through.
'Carers hold families together through some of the toughest moments dementia can bring.
'Now we need to be there for them.
'We are enormously grateful to the Daily Mail, Mail Force and every reader who supports this appeal and helps us make sure fewer carers have to face dementia alone.'
The survey for the Mail found 72 per cent of the public believe carers get too little recognition, 72 per cent feel they receive too little help for their own physical and mental health needs and 66 per cent say they have too little financial support.
Asked for the three places they would be most likely to turn for help if a loved one was diagnosed with dementia, 56 per cent said their GP, 51 per cent dementia charities and 41 per cent the internet.
The issues they would most want advice on are slowing or managing symptoms (38 per cent), how to keep the patient safe at home (38 per cent) and how to get NHS or council support (32 per cent).
All these topics will be covered in the new Dementia Carers Together courses.
Almost two in three people (64 per cent) were not aware they would be entitled to a carer's assessment, a free check carried out by local councils to establish what emotional, physical or financial help carers themselves may need to support them in their caring responsibilities.
Meanwhile, one in eight (12 per cent) wrongly believe the NHS or government always pays for a dementia patient's care in full and one in five (21 per cent) are not sure.
Tragically, only 62 per cent of people would feel comfortable telling close friends if they were struggling to cope with someone with dementia and only 64 per cent would feel comfortable telling family.
The biggest barriers are not wanting to burden others (43 per cent), feeling guilty about struggling (31 per cent) and not knowing where to turn (30 per cent).
Only 16 per cent say they would not be reluctant to ask for help.
The campaign is aiming to raise a minimum of £1million, which will pay for the courses for a year. If it reaches £2million the courses can run for two years, or for three years if it generates £3million.
Each course will have roughly 30 participants, meaning tens of thousands of people could benefit in the first year alone.
Dementia Carers Together pilot courses will launch in London, Peterborough, Wales and Northern Ireland once the appeal passes £100,000.
The 2027 courses will open for booking from the New Year. Those in Scotland will be delivered via Alzheimer Scotland.
:: YouGov polled 2,328 UK adults online between October 25 and 26.
Dementia Carers Together is raising money to fund new courses across the UK to give tens of thousands of struggling unpaid dementia carers vital emotional and practical support.
For further information, visit dailymail.com/dementia

articles.title_orig: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
articles.title_zh: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic announced new workplace features on Tuesday, including Claude Meetings, which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking. The company also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets.
The launch of Anthropic’s new productivity-focused features comes just a few weeks after OpenAI unveiled a series of workplace tools that allow users to collaborate with ChatGPT to do things like visualize company information and create presentations, as both companies compete to turn their products into office suites of sorts to take on Microsoft and Google. Meta is also joining the competition with its Muse AI agent, which can build mini-apps on the fly to help users complete specific tasks.
With Claude Meetings, teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant. Claude then follows the conversation and gets to work on tasks in real time. As participants talk, it can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year’s figures. After the call, the meeting notes, action items, and other materials Claude created are available in claude.ai.
The work that comes out of a meeting usually starts after everyone hangs up, but with this new feature, teams can turn discussions into actions in real time, Anthropic says.
Claude identifies itself as a meeting participant and posts a notice in the meeting chat. It won’t join calls with external guests unless authorized by an admin, and will automatically leave if an external guest joins.
Claude Meetings is launching in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. At launch, it works with Google Meet, with support for additional plans expected to follow.
As for Claude Whiteboards, Anthropic describes the feature as a collaborative board where teams can talk through a plan and have Claude turn it into an organized visual workspace with timelines and deadlines.
The company notes that many people already brainstorm with Claude, but that in order to share their results with others, they would have to copy-paste them somewhere else. Now, a team can work directly with Claude on the same board in real time.
When the brainstorm is done, Claude can turn the board into a doc or a slide deck. Additionally, Whiteboards also work inside Claude Meetings, so the board builds while people talk, Anthropic says.
Claude Whiteboards is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop, and mobile.
The company also launched Claude Sheets, which lets teams create and collaboratively edit spreadsheets with Claude. A team can ask it to build a campaign tracker or hiring budget, and Claude will then generate a working spreadsheet.
Anthropic says Claude handles the initial setup of trackers and budgets, while allowing teams to continue refining and updating the same spreadsheet. Each spreadsheet can include multiple tabs, formulas, formatting, and dropdown menus. Claude also makes edits directly in cells alongside the team, and outlines each change so users can see what it did.
Claude Sheets is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop and mobile.
Anthropic also announced that Claude Data, formerly known as Claude Dashboards, is now generally available. The feature connects Claude to systems that companies use to keep their numbers, like a data warehouse or CRM. Users can ask questions, and Claude responds with dashboards, written data stories, or narrated videos.
Additionally, the company announced interactive connectors that open the full version of apps like Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot inside Claude. Anthropic notes that teams can now open these apps directly alongside their Claude conversations and ask the assistant to work within them, essentially bringing existing workflows into the same workspace.

articles.title_orig: Google Fi brings back network switching with ‘secondary’ partner, expands W+ beyond Pixel
articles.title_zh: Google Fi brings back network switching with ‘secondary’ partner, expands W+ beyond Pixel
articles.content_orig:
Google Fi Wireless is rolling out a big update today with the return of network switching thanks to a “secondary” partner.
At the beginning, Project Fi was known for giving subscribers access to both T-Mobile and Sprint networks. Over time, the second partner went away, leaving one predominant network.
Google Fi is now bringing back a second partner as part of its new “super network.” Most users will be on the “Primary network,” but Google Fi will automatically switch users to the “Secondary network” if it meaningfully improves performance with so-called “smart thresholds” for doing so. At launch, there is no manual switching.
Google is not naming the second network today, but did share that Ultra Wideband is supported. Officially, you are switching between “two of America’s fastest 5G networks.”
Fi Wireless does note that users have top priority, so data is never deprioritized on the Primary network. Meanwhile, there’s “highest QCI priority” on the backup network that means subscribers are among the last to be slowed down when there’s congestion. This is also available internationally when local partner networks are available with the Flexible and Unlimited Premium plans.
Network switching will first be supported on Pixel 9 and newer devices that have a Google Fi eSIM (and no other SIM active). It makes use of Android’s Multiple Enabled Profiles (MEP) eSIM technology that allows for two carrier profiles on a single chip.
The Google Fi app gains a “Your super network” card in the Home tab that shows whether you’re connected to the Primary or Secondary network. “See activity” lets you view switching history and when it last occurred. Google will also note if you’re in range of W+ networks.
Google today is also expanding its Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ network beyond Pixel phones to select Samsung Galaxy (S23, Fold/Flip 5, and newer) and modern Motorola phones. These premium Wi-Fi networks are available in millions of airports, malls, stores, and restaurants. The connection happens automatically, with the Google Fi Virtual Carrier Network encrypting data.
The final update today sees the companion app gain “Ask Fi.” This AI-powered chat is meant to quickly provide answers and guided troubleshooting for common issues. You can request human support with seamless handoff that keeps the chat context.
These Google Fi updates start rolling out today, with network switching seeing gradual availability. This launch is accompanied by several deals:

articles.title_orig: Credit card debt climbs to a record $1.29 trillion, New York Fed research finds
articles.title_zh: Credit card debt climbs to a record $1.29 trillion, New York Fed research finds
articles.content_orig:
Americans are increasingly turning to credit cards as financial pressures mount, new reports show.
Collectively, credit card balances climbed by $22 billion in the third quarter to a record $1.29 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's latest household debt report , released Tuesday. Balances are up 4.2% from a year earlier.
Total household debt, including mortgages , auto loans and student loans , also expanded by $334 billion for the July-to-September period to a record $19.1 trillion.
"Overall debt has been growing," the New York Fed researchers said on a press call Tuesday. "This does reflect financial hardship out there."
The average credit card balance per consumer now stands at $6,678, up 2.4% year over year, a separate quarterly credit industry insights report from TransUnion found. The number of people with credit cards rose 2% to 178 million from 174.8 million.
Consumers often turn to credit cards in part because they are more accessible than other types of loans — even though the average interest rate on a new credit card offer is about 24%, according to data from LendingTree . Credit card APRs vary depending on the type of card, the issuer and the borrower's creditworthiness.
"Credit cards continue to be one of the most expensive ways to borrow," said Charlie Wise, TransUnion's senior vice president of global research and consulting.
Over time, an increasing share of new credit cards has gone to borrowers with lower incomes and credit scores, and "those accounts are now showing higher levels of distress," the New York Fed researchers said in a corresponding blog post .
Credit card issuers loosened their lending standards during the Covid pandemic, and delinquency rates rose in the years that followed, the New York Fed researchers said on the press call.
"Macroeconomic headwinds — namely high inflation and rising borrowing costs — have squeezed consumers, with inflation outpacing wage growth for low-income brackets," according to the New York Fed.
Meanwhile, the cost of living continues to climb, with Americans paying more for essentials such as groceries and gas.
Stubborn inflation has now stretched on for years, putting many households in an affordability squeeze. Costs for goods and services rose more than expected again in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics also reported Tuesday.
"Higher prices and higher rates have pushed more people into debt," said Ted Rossman, principal consumer finance analyst at Money Management International, a nonprofit credit counseling agency.
Balances have continued to swell in the wake of the pandemic, and even though the growth rate is now slowing, "from a household finance standpoint, a lot of damage has been done," Rossman said.
The reports come on the heels of the Democrats' strong midterm results, when many voters expressed their dissatisfaction with the U.S. economy , according to Kyle Moore, chief economist at the nonpartisan think tank The Century Foundation.
"The throughline connecting so many of Tuesday's outcomes was a recognition that the American economy is failing American families," Moore said, referring to Election Day.

articles.title_orig: Why Did Moscow Police Just Arrest Scores of Teenagers?
articles.title_zh: Why Did Moscow Police Just Arrest Scores of Teenagers?
articles.content_orig:
In Moscow, Russia — an aggressor state — the Tagansky District Court sentenced 21-year-old local resident Magomed Gasanov to 13 days of administrative arrest under Article 19.3 of Russia’s Code of Administrative Offenses. This was reported by Meduza , citing the outlet Ostorozhno, Novosti.
Gasanov was detained on November 7 and taken to the Tagansky police station. A report drawn up by police officers alleges that he refused to show his passport and get into a police van.
The court received the report on November 9 and considered the case the same day. In court, Gasanov partially admitted guilt but denied failing to comply with police officers’ demands. According to him, he “did not immediately understand what was happening.”
More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram .
Ostorozhno, Novosti believes that Gasanov was detained during police raids in the Kitay-gorod area. On the evening of November 7, police detained hundreds of teenagers and young people near Gorka Park on Bolshoy Spasoglinishchevsky Lane.
Those detained reported that at police stations they were offered contracts for military service, while some were handed draft notices. On November 9, a total of 12 reports for minor hooliganism or disobeying police were submitted to the Basmanny and Tagansky district courts. It is currently unknown whether these cases are connected to the detentions in Kitay-gorod.

articles.title_orig: Pixel Tag tidbits: Surprise NFC, Find Hub setup, & Bellroy keychain cases
articles.title_zh: Pixel Tag tidbits: Surprise NFC, Find Hub setup, & Bellroy keychain cases
articles.content_orig:
The Made by Google 2026 lineup is finally complete with tomorrow’s retail launch of the Pixel Tag . You can find our review here , while there are some additional details about the device since the August announcement.
The Pixel Tag is the first Find Hub tracker with NFC. Google did not mention this connectivity specification in August, with Near Field Communication letting you tap the tracker to the back of your phone to immediately open device settings. The NFC area on the Pixel Tag is below the circular battery door, which you hold down and twist counterclockwise to open.
On Android 17 QPR2, tapping immediately opens the details page. On QPR1, you first get a system notification that you need to click. NFC joins Bluetooth 6.0 with Channel Sounding and Ultra Wideband (UWB).
The setup process adds a new screen after the initial pairing and terms of use. It lets you configure: Notify when left behind, Ring this phone, Edit name, Edit category, and Adjust volume for this tag.
The Pixel Tag has a physical button on the rear side below the battery cover. Clicking twice plays a loud sound on your phone if both devices are nearby. Once found, you can tap the button once to silence, or turn it off from your phone. This feature can be disabled from the Pixel Tag’s device details page on a tracker-by-tracker basis.
Google does not have a first-party case for the Pixel Tag. Instead, it’s working with Made for Google partner Bellroy.
There are two models available from the Google Store, with the first made of silicone. The Bellroy Lite Case Duo costs $24.99 and comes in a pack of two: Mist and Shadow colorways. It wraps everything but the face of the Pixel Tag (and its speaker cutout), while giving you a hole in the corner and color-matching cord.
There’s also the Bellroy Leather Tag Case in Artichoke, Azalea, Black, Pewter, and Red Ochre for $29.99.
